answers.answer: Each player takes twelve ordinary turns: three ordinary rounds in each of four seasons. Courtship rounds have no player turns, service rotation, monument income, or Servants’ Hall use.
answers.evidence: Overview: ‘each player takes twelve ordinary turns’; courtship has ‘no player turns, service rotation, monument income or Servants’ Hall use.’

answers.answer: Hosting order: rotate Quarters servants to Available, then Expended servants to Quarters (each advances one space); resolve the round-track event; resolve applicable monument and Servants’ Hall effects in either order; choose an activity tile; invite the exact required gentry; provide each required service; collect all favours, resolving positive before negative; optionally buy; then clear up. At cleanup, servants used in any capacity go to Expended Service, played gentry go to your personal discard, and return the activity tile to its tableau column, flipping/upgrading as required. Only the last player in turn order advances the round marker one space after cleanup.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure / Hosting an activity; Player Reference: ‘rotate service → event → ongoing effects → choose tile → invite exact gentry → staff tile/cards → positive then negative favours → buy’ and cleanup destinations.

answers.answer: Passing order: send all servants directly to Available Service; return all gentry in your discard to hand; resolve the round-track event and then ongoing tile effects; choose £200 or a free Market refresh; optionally buy one tile; last player advances the marker. Servants used for ongoing effects are expended at turn end. Butler’s Room hiring is an activity and cannot be taken as a passing benefit.
answers.evidence: Passing: ‘all servants directly to Available Service → all gentry in your discard to hand → round-track event, then ongoing tile effects → choose £200 or a free Market refresh → optional one tile purchase.’

answers.answer: Yes. The activity and guests are screened at the fixed end-of-step-2 reputation, 6.1, before Choose Activity. Service Help can be used four times, spending three increments each time; it moves one servant per action from Servants’ Quarters to Available Service, never from Expended Service. The later actual reputation of 3.4 does not invalidate the activity or attendees.
answers.evidence: Reputation screening is fixed ‘at the end of step 2, before Choose Activity’ and remains screening level for the whole activity; Service Help moves one servant from Quarters to Available for 3 increments, repeatable.

answers.answer: Resolve all positive favours before all negative favours; order within either group is your choice. At minimum reputation, you cannot take a negative reputation favour first to shelter it: a negative reputation favour cannot take you below 1.1, but the rule says positive favours resolve first. A money penalty must be fully payable; use positive activity money favours, a money VP card, or Borrow Money. If short, borrow if possible; if payment still cannot be funded, you cannot play that guest or tile.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 6: ‘positive favours before all negative favours’; money penalty must be fully payable, with listed funding options.

answers.answer: Borrow Money costs 2 reputation increments and gains £100; repeatable. Service Help costs 3 increments and moves one servant from Quarters to Available; repeatable. Refresh Market costs 4 increments and fully refreshes the Market; special-action refresh is once per turn. At minimum reputation (1.1), you cannot take a special action. Service Help cannot take a servant directly from Expended Service.
answers.evidence: Special actions table and minimum-reputation rule: Borrow Money 2; Service Help 3; Refresh Market 4 (once per turn); Service Help cannot take from Expended.

answers.answer: Host Servant Hiring from the Butler’s Room using an available butler or underbutler and no gentry. Take up to two servants from Servants for Hire, excluding underbutlers, into Expended Service; there is no fee. The upgraded room instead allows recruiting one common servant (footman, valet, or lady’s maid) from any location on one opponent’s family board into your Expended Service, instead of taking up to two from supply. No gentry may attend.
answers.evidence: Butler’s Room paragraph gives the required servant, ‘no gentry,’ quantity, source, destination, no fee, and upgraded recruiting alternative.

answers.answer: A housekeeper can substitute for a lady’s maid only when no lady’s maids are available. With a Brushing Room in your tableau, footmen can substitute for valets only when no valets are available. An underbutler can substitute for any base male servant (butler, valet, footman) even if that servant type is available.
answers.evidence: Servants and hiring: substitution rules for housekeeper, Brushing Room footmen, and underbutler.

answers.answer: The only way to acquire an underbutler is to purchase Butler’s Pantry; take one from supply immediately into Expended Service. Normally it moves to Quarters at your next rotation and Available Service at your second subsequent rotation; passing or a Refresh Service VP card can make it available sooner, and once in Quarters Service Help or the Servants’ Quarters tile can permit earlier use. Another player cannot recruit it because it is unique, not common.
answers.evidence: Butler’s Pantry paragraph: only acquisition route, immediate destination, subsequent rotations, early-use exceptions, and opponent recruitment prohibition.

answers.answer: Market price is the price printed for its space plus the tile’s printed price modifier. Reserve base price is £300 plus the modifier. The price cannot fall below £100. You cannot acquire a duplicate of a tile you already own. Reputation does not restrict purchasing, so a tile above your reputation may be bought.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Market and Reserve: price formulas, £100 floor, no duplicates, and reputation does not restrict purchasing.

answers.answer: When a Market space empties, slide remaining tiles left and draw replacements into rightmost spaces. A drawn duplicate stacks on its matching Market tile and you draw again; duplicates share one space and its price. Qualifying Reserve tiles go straight to Reserve and you draw again. If filling multiple spaces, sort only newly drawn tiles by ascending sorting number. Buying one tile from a two-tile duplicate stack leaves that space occupied, so no refill occurs.
answers.evidence: Refill paragraph explains sliding, duplicate stacks/re-draw, Reserve-eligible draws, sorting, and one-from-stack behavior.

answers.answer: After courtship 1, move all Market Service tiles except Largest Wine Cellar to Reserve; future Service draws also go directly there except Largest Wine Cellar. After courtship 2, move all Market PR1 tiles to Reserve and future PR1 draws go directly there. Largest Wine Cellar never enters Reserve. Full Market refresh is standard after each of the first three courtships, after Reserve movement.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve and Refresh sections; Overview says full seasonal Market refresh is standard in this compendium.

answers.answer: At an ordinary courtship, first return both Fairchilds to Alderley Hall. For courtships 1–3, score the current theme’s tile VP, including negatives; only the face-up hybrid category counts. Highest scorer gets one VP card and chooses one Fairchild for hand. Each tied-high player draws one VP card and no one gets a Fairchild. Every player discards one objective; shuffle simultaneous discards together and put them on the bottom of the objective deck. After courtships 1–3, pass the first-player marker anticlockwise (after Reserve opening, Market refresh, and revealing the next theme).
answers.evidence: Courtship and seasonal upkeep specifies Fairchild return, theme scoring, tie outcome, objective discard, and upkeep order/direction.

answers.answer: At final courtship, return both Fairchilds and total tile VP for all four revealed themes; repeated categories count each time. Highest score gets one VP card and a Fairchild. Ties break by highest reputation level, ignoring wheel position; if still tied, no Fairchild is awarded and tied winners draw VP cards under the tie rule. Discard the final objective. Before scoring, players get a final chance to use special actions and VP cards for benefits where possible; then move the marker to Wedding Bells and score. The final Fairchild winner keeps its 8 VP.
answers.evidence: Final courtship paragraph gives scoring, tie sequence, objective discard, final benefits, Wedding Bells and retained Fairchild scoring.

answers.answer: End-game categories: all improvement-tile face-up VP (including negative and unused); gentry VP in hand and discard (including family, negatives and final Fairchild; dismissed guests excluded); fulfilled remaining objectives; reputation level; servants; wealth; retained unused VP cards. Reputation levels 1–7 score 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, 21, 28 VP. Wealth is 1 VP per £200, rounded down. Highest total wins; ties go to the player with the final Fairchild, then highest reputation level; if still tied, share victory.
answers.evidence: Final VP table and tie paragraph list all scoring categories, reputation values, wealth rounding and tiebreaks.

answers.answer: Normally each player gets five objectives at setup and draws two on round 6; one is discarded at each of four courtships, leaving three to score. Main Library or an Objective VP card can add objectives to the retained final count without an extra discard. Shuffle simultaneous courtship discards together, then put them face down on the bottom of the objective deck. Tile objectives require owning the named tiles at game end; upgrading them is not required.
answers.evidence: Objectives and VP cards: ‘five at setup plus two on round 6’; discard one at each of four courtships; tile ownership does not require upgrading.

answers.answer: A VP card may be used immediately when drawn, at any time on your later turn (several cards allowed), and once more after final courtship before scoring. Reveal and discard it to use its benefit; used VP cards go to the bottom of the VP deck. Retained cards score their printed VP at game end. You cannot take both benefit and VP from one card.
answers.evidence: VP card paragraph states use timing, discard destination, and retained-card scoring choice.

answers.answer: A normal activity tile must flip to its rose/upgrade side after first use at cleanup. An already-upgraded normal tile stays upgraded on later uses. Hybrids have no rose: begin with underlined category showing, flip after every use, and move to the newly face-up category. A tile that upgrades into an ongoing monument (Queen’s Suite or Lionheart Suite) has only its front-side activity use; after it upgrades it can never host again, and monument benefits begin on subsequent turns. Only the currently face-up hybrid category counts at courtship and for objectives.
answers.evidence: Improvements and ongoing effects describes mandatory flips, hybrid alternation/category, and suites’ one activity use and later monument state.

answers.answer: Monuments give one reputation per ordinary turn during the ongoing-effects step, whether hosting or passing; no income during courtship, and a newly purchased monument first pays on a later turn. Servants’ Hall works in the same hosting/pass ongoing-effects step: place one available servant on it, reduce one opponent’s reputation by one and gain one yourself; that servant cannot serve the activity and goes to Expended Service at turn end. You may not target a player at minimum reputation.
answers.evidence: Monuments and Servants’ Hall effects specify timings, amount, servant use/destination and minimum-reputation restriction.

answers.answer: Heritage Guest Suite requires one footman on the tile and one casual guest from hand, with the guest’s normal service; it doubles all that guest’s favours, including negatives, then upgrades and remains an activity tile. Queen’s Suite requires a housekeeper and one prestige guest from hand with normal service; it doubles one chosen favour and resolves other favours normally, then upgrades into a monument. Lionheart Suite requires a butler and draws one prestige guest from the deck to attend without personal guest service; it doubles nonnegative favours, not negative ones, and the guest is kept and put in discard at cleanup; the suite upgrades into a monument. Each has a fixed one-guest count that cannot be changed.
answers.evidence: Suite activity table and following fixed-count rule.

answers.answer: A random player receives the first-player marker. Starting with that player’s left, players choose available base family boards clockwise. Bonuses: Asquith gets the Dowager Countess as a fifth family card; Cavendish starts at reputation 1.4; Ponsonby gains £300; York gets an extra footman in Available Service.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 1 and 5.

answers.answer: Each player starts at reputation level 1, position 1, with the 1/2 counter showing in the 1/2, 3/4, 5/6, Max stack; 7/8 counters are not used. Each gets one butler, housekeeper, valet, lady’s maid and footman in Available Service; Private Study, Butler’s Room, Main Gazebo, Front Parlour and Bowling Green with starter/building icon showing; and Lord, Lady, Heir and Young Lady family cards. Only Ponsonby starts with money (£300); the others have no money, though Cavendish and York have their own listed bonuses.
answers.evidence: Setup steps 2, 3, and 5.

answers.answer: For three players, put three valets, three lady’s maids, six footmen, and two underbutlers total in Servants for Hire. No butlers or housekeepers are stocked there. Unused servants are returned to the box and are unavailable this game.
answers.evidence: Setup step 6: one valet and lady’s maid per player, two footmen per player, two underbutlers total; no butlers or housekeepers; unused servants unavailable.

answers.answer: Separate starter guests from the casual deck, shuffle them, and deal two to each player. Shuffle every unused starter back into the casual deck. During play starter guests are casual guests with a starter icon and otherwise follow normal casual rules.
answers.evidence: Setup step 4 and Gentry section.

answers.answer: For four players, select five double-sided monuments (one per player plus one). Choose at most one of Sculpture Garden and Garden Maze. Selected monuments and all nonstarter base improvement tiles go in the draw bag. Tiles that later upgrade into monuments also go in the bag and do not count against the setup selection.
answers.evidence: Setup step 7.

answers.answer: The opening Market has six different eligible tiles: PR3 or less (including no PR), not Servants’ Hall, and not a double-sided monument. Draw until six eligible spaces are filled; set ineligible draws aside and return them to the bag after filling; stack duplicate eligible tiles in one space. Normal tiles enter with upgrade/rose icon hidden; hybrids with the underlined hybrid icon showing. Sort the six spaces by ascending sorting number from the £300 space. PR4 tiles, Servants’ Hall and double-sided monuments are ineligible.
answers.evidence: Setup step 8.

answers.answer: Place Alderley Hall standard side up, round marker at 1, and one reminder token per player above the track. Shuffle theme and VP decks separately; reveal the first theme for open courtship and keep revealed themes in order through the game. Put base Charles and Elizabeth Fairchild face up on Alderley Hall. The first theme is revealed, not hidden, and old revealed themes stay in play/order as additional themes are revealed.
answers.evidence: Setup step 9 and Overview courtship scope.

answers.answer: At the start of a hosting turn, Quarters servants move to Available Service first; then Expended servants move to Quarters, each advancing one space. So the servant in Quarters becomes Available and the servant in Expended becomes Quarters. An unused Available servant remains available.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 1; service table: all Quarters move first, then all Expended move; unused available servants remain available.

answers.answer: No immediate Village Fair reward is gained: the event resolves before activity selection, and the Private Study must already be upgraded at that step. You may host its activity later that turn, but that does not retroactively earn the reward. An already-upgraded Study gives £300 and 2 reputation. Village Fair spaces are 3 and 9.
answers.evidence: Round-track table: spaces 3 and 9; reward only if Private Study is already upgraded at event step.

answers.answer: Resolve Draw Objectives as the round-track event before ongoing effects: on space 6 draw two objectives and keep both secret with your other objectives. It happens during passing as well as hosting because both resolve the event; passing does not exempt a player.
answers.evidence: Round-track events section says space 6 draws two objectives and events resolve during hosting and passing; passing order resolves event.

answers.answer: Yes. On National Holiday (space 14), ignore PR on all tiles and guests when hosting, so low reputation can play higher-PR ones. All other requirements remain binding, including service and exact gentry counts/types.
answers.evidence: Round-track table: National Holiday ignores PR but still obeys all other requirements, including service and gentry counts/types.

answers.answer: Yes, buy any number from the Market and/or Reserve within funds. Finish all purchases before sliding/refilling; use the single unchanged Market and original prices (space or Reserve price plus printed modifier) applying before the first purchase. Do not slide/refill or refresh between purchases. Refill resulting empty spaces together after the sequence. A Market Purchase VP-card benefit follows the same Builders’ Holiday rules and same no-refresh-between-purchases restriction.
answers.evidence: Builders’ Holiday / Market Purchase VP card paragraph.

answers.answer: Set all Market tiles aside while refilling all six spaces under normal rules; they cannot reappear during that same refresh. Leave Reserve tiles unchanged. After the six replacements are drawn and sorted, return the set-aside Market tiles to the bag and mix.
answers.evidence: Refresh paragraph: set all Market tiles aside, leave Reserve unchanged, refill, then return set-aside tiles to bag.

answers.answer: Each reputation symbol is one increment. Moving clockwise gains and anticlockwise loses; passing wheel position 5 to 1 raises a level, while passing 1 to 5 lowers a level. Minimum is 1.1 and maximum in standard play is 7.5 (Max.5); losses beyond minimum are ignored. At Max.5, excess reputation is lost unless spent immediately on special actions; you can take special actions before or during a reputation favour to make room.
answers.evidence: Reputation, wealth and special actions section.

answers.answer: Money held is public. Players may not give or receive money between one another in this mode. Never spend more money than you have. The common supply is unlimited; use proxies if needed.
answers.evidence: Money held paragraph.

answers.answer: Ladies includes every female family member or female guest, so family members may fill ladies requirements. Gentlemen likewise includes male family members or male guests. A requirement for two casual guests requires two casual guests and excludes family. You must meet the exact printed count and types; no extra gentry may be played. Family needs no personal service and has no PR threshold.
answers.evidence: Hosting step 4 states gender categories include family, casual/prestige requirements exclude family, exact number/types required; reputation section says family has no PR and family needs no personal service.

answers.answer: An ordinary guest-invite favour draws one card from the indicated deck, reveals it to everyone, and adds it to your hand; explicit larger counts override one. For screening, draw the stated number and choose the stated number to keep; reveal only kept cards and add them to hand. Put rejected screened cards on the bottom of their guest deck without revealing them.
answers.evidence: Gentry section distinguishes ordinary invite and screening guests.

answers.answer: Dismissal is always optional, so you need not dismiss anyone. You may dismiss an eligible guest from hand, the current activity, or discard, including one just drawn earlier in Enjoy Favours. Family cannot be dismissed. Put the guest on the bottom of its matching deck; it is no longer yours, does not return on passing, and does not score later.
answers.evidence: Dismissal paragraph.

answers.answer: Lord: £200. Lady: choose screening two casual guests and keeping one, or optionally dismiss one guest. Heir: choose £100 or one reputation. Asquith Dowager: both £100 and one reputation. Lady and Heir offer a choice; Asquith gives both, while Lord gives a single benefit.
answers.evidence: Base family card favour table.

answers.answer: The admirer bonus applies only when a male prestige guest attends; it does not apply to a male casual guest or a female prestige guest. Charles Fairchild is a male prestige guest, so he qualifies. The bonus is two reputation, and Young Lady still draws one casual guest in all cases.
answers.evidence: Young Lady table entry; Charles is identified as male, and both Fairchilds are prestige guests.

answers.answer: Charles is a male prestige guest with no PR; he requires a valet and gives three reputation. Elizabeth is a female prestige guest with no PR; she requires a lady’s maid and gives both one prestige guest and two reputation. Neither has family-card dismissal immunity: both are guests and may be dismissed normally.
answers.evidence: Gentry section identifies genders, type, PR, service, favours, and dismissal status.

answers.answer: Miss Elizabeth Perkins reduces one opponent’s reputation by one. Miss Florence Oliver reduces one opponent by two and makes you lose one yourself. Minimum-reputation protection applies, so a player at 1.1 cannot be targeted by an opponent’s reputation-reducing effect.
answers.evidence: Gentry gossip description and minimum-reputation protection.

answers.answer: The Barn gives one reputation each time you host an Estate activity. Merely owning an Estate tile gives none, and passing gives none.
answers.evidence: Barn: ‘every time you host an Estate activity, gain one reputation’; no reward for owning an Estate tile or passing.

answers.answer: Ordinary rotation moves all Quarters servants to Available, then all Expended servants to Quarters, one space each at the start of a hosting turn, without reputation cost. The Servants’ Quarters improvement lets you use one servant still in Quarters after rotation directly, in addition to Available Service, once per ordinary turn, with no reputation cost; send it to Expended at turn end. Service Help instead costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves one Quarters servant to Available (not from Expended); it is repeatable.
answers.evidence: Service mechanism table and Service Help description.

answers.answer: The Private Study’s front activity requires two family and a butler; it has no tile favour and upgrades after first use into an ongoing tile. Once upgraded it cannot be hosted again. It gives £300 and two reputation only on Village Fair rounds (spaces 3 and 9), without staffing or hosting it again.
answers.evidence: Private Study paragraph and round-track event table.

answers.answer: Before upgrading, Main Library requires a butler and two family and draws one extra objective. After upgrading it requires a butler and three family and draws one VP card. Extra objectives increase the number retained for final scoring; they do not cause an extra courtship discard.
answers.evidence: Main Library paragraph; Objectives section says extra objectives add to final retained count without extra discard.

answers.answer: The Objective VP card draws two objectives, keeps one, and returns the other to the bottom of the objective deck. It gives one additional retained objective for final scoring.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit table: Objective draws two, keep one, return other to bottom; adds one retained objective.

answers.answer: Yes. Refresh Service moves all servants directly to Available Service, including those in Expended Service, and they are usable immediately. Service Help costs 3 reputation increments per servant and moves only one servant from Quarters to Available; it cannot take directly from Expended.
answers.evidence: Refresh Service VP card and comparison with Service Help.

answers.answer: A Hire Servant VP card takes one servant from Servants for Hire (not underbutler) into Expended Service. The servant cannot provide service immediately from Expended Service; ordinary service rotation advances Expended servants to Quarters, then Available on a subsequent rotation.
answers.evidence: VP-card benefit: hire goes into Expended Service; the service table says Expended servants move to Quarters at rotation and only Available servants (or one servant still in Quarters via the tile) can be used.

answers.answer: Yes, Refresh Guest may return a family member from your personal discard to hand. If it is returned before Invite Gentry, you may choose it to attend that turn, subject to normal requirements. Returning it does not automatically play it; it must be selected during attendee selection.
answers.evidence: Refresh Guest VP card benefit paragraph.

answers.answer: The basic-servant objective counts only common footmen, valets, and lady’s maids; it excludes butler, housekeeper, and underbutler. Ordinary servant VP scores 2 VP for every servant in your employ, all types and locations. The ten-servant objective gives 7 VP for at least ten servants total, without the basic-servant restriction stated for that objective.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference says basic-servant counts only common types; Final VP counts all servants; Servant sets lists 7 VP for at least ten total.

answers.answer: Yes. Upgraded Queen’s Suite and Lionheart Suite count as monuments for the monument objective, worth 3 VP per monument. Category objectives count monuments and hybrids currently in their category; for a hybrid, only its currently face-up category counts.
answers.evidence: Objective reference: category bonus counts monuments and hybrids currently in category; monument objective includes upgraded Queen’s and Lionheart Suites; hybrid rule uses face-up category.

answers.answer: Nature Group is 11 VP for Flower Room plus one of English Garden, French Garden, Sculpture Garden, or Garden Maze. Domestic Group is 12 VP for Gabled Conservatory plus one of Main Library or North Library. Owning the required tiles at game end is enough; they need not have been used or upgraded.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference lists both group requirements and says use/upgrading is unnecessary.

answers.answer: Guest objectives exclude family. The prestige-guest bonus counts prestige guests, including a final Fairchild. The every-three-guests objective counts all nonfamily guests; an incomplete group of three scores nothing because it scores one VP per complete three guests.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference: ‘Guest excludes family’; prestige guests include final Fairchild; 1 VP per complete three guests.

answers.answer: The reputation objective scores 7 VP for reaching maximum reputation level 7, regardless of wheel position. The wealth objective scores 10 VP for at least £1200. Wheel position does not affect ordinary reputation VP or reputation tiebreaks; ordinary VP uses level only, and tiebreaks use reputation level.
answers.evidence: Base objective reference and Final VP: max level 7 regardless of wheel position; wealth at least £1200; wheel position has no effect on VP or ties.

answers.answer: Both sides require one butler and exactly three family cards. Before upgrading, its favour is to draw one prestige guest. After upgrading, it draws one prestige guest and may optionally dismiss one to four guests from hand, current activity, or discard to the bottoms of their decks. West Terrace remains an activity on both sides; it does not become an ongoing dismissal tile.
answers.evidence: West Terrace paragraph.

answers.answer: There is no maximum hand or personal discard size. Gentry in your discard pile still belong to you and score normally; passing returns them to your hand.
answers.evidence: Gentry section: no hand/discard limit; discard-pile gentry score normally and passing recovers them.

answers.answer: You may inspect all Reserve tiles at any time and buy any one, including one underneath another in a stack; there is no top-tile-only restriction. Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection.
answers.evidence: Open Reserve: ‘Every Reserve tile is public and available for selection. You may inspect all tiles at any time and buy any one … including a tile underneath another in a stack.’

answers.answer: You may choose to host or pass; you are not required to host whenever able. If your preferred activity lacks required gentry or service, choose another legal activity or pass. If no activity is possible, you must pass.
answers.evidence: Turn Structure offers ‘host an activity or pass’; Hosting step 5 says choose another legal activity or pass, and if none is possible, must pass.

answers.answer: Yes. On a passing turn, you may take the free Market refresh benefit, also use the once-per-turn paid special-action Market refresh (4 reputation increments), and use multiple Market Refresh VP cards, each for a separate full refresh, subject to purchase-timing restrictions. The once-per-turn limit applies only to the special-action refresh; passing-benefit and VP-card refreshes have separate availability.
answers.evidence: Special actions section states free pass refresh and VP refreshes do not use the special refresh allowance; multiple Market Refresh VP cards are allowed; one paid special refresh per turn.
